newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Ciech to offer 36 pct to large investors.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Ciech to offer 36 pct to large investors.

text.p: Poland's largest chemicals trader Ciech SA wants to offer up to 36 percent of its shares to large investors through the planned initial public offering approved by shareholders last year, the firm's spokesman said on Friday.
Marek Kwiatkowski told Reuters that Ciech employees would be offered up to six million shares or 15 percent of the company through the new issue.
He said the firm expects to float 23 percent of the company on the Warsaw bourse, while Ciech's current shareholders would keep 26 percent, or 10,525,216 shares.
The bourse tranche would come from stock currently owned by the treasury and the 36 percent for large investors amounted to 14.2 million shares, to be offered ex-rights, Kwiatkowski said.
The public offering was approved by Ciech shareholders on December 24, 1996.

Earlier that month Ciech's President Zdzislaw Matkiewicz said the company planned to raise 200-400 million zlotys from the new issue and hoped for a Warsaw bourse listing in the second quarter of 1997.
The state treasury currently holds about 51 percent of Ciech with the rest owned by numerous, mostly state-owned companies in the chemical sector.
Ciech expected to make a 51-million-zloty net profit in 1996 against 50 million zlotys in 1995 and 48 million in 1994.
The firm, which ranks among Poland's largest companies, expected sales to rise 15.3 percent in 1996 from $960 million in 1995 and $1.3 billion in 1994.
